propositions: A check whose PASS result is indistinguishable from never having run — via absence assertion on subprocess/file/network output with no producer-liveness verification — cannot distinguish its verdict from its own failure and must be detected as a fail-open oracle antipattern.

The same broken instrument can produce a confident FAILING result for a reason other than the condition (e.g., wrong input, producer emitted nothing), creating a false alarm that is more likely to be believed and acted upon than a silent pass.

Nine instances of fail-open defects split across two populations: five in shipped rebar code (error-handling host: pgrep self-match, unchecked returncode, silent lookup miss) and four in test code (tests host: absence grep on colorized output, convergence twin, truncated log, child output).

The fail-open/producer-liveness detection language must be added to the existing tests criterion (test-oracle population) and error-handling criterion (shipped-code population), not as a new criterion, per operator ruling and calibration validation.

Calibration replay confirmed 9/9 pre-fix cases fire with quoted claims naming the seeded fail-open defect, and 9/9 post-fix cases yield zero findings, validating reliable language placement in both hosts.
Documentation of the pattern with two worked examples must be added to rebar explain review (src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md) since code-review criteria lack per-criterion explain surfaces.
